column_audit.correction_to_the_premise: The brief says 'the only loading feature is the scenario scalar agg_loading'. That is not right: agg_loading is listed in make_splits.EXCLUDE_COLS and is therefore NOT a feature. The committed design matrix carries NO loading information of any kind. It does carry vm0_* (118 pre-outage bus voltages), so part of the base AC solution is already exposed - the voltages, not the flows.

acceptance.tolerance_note: reconstruction is accepted only if max|vm error| < 1e-6

CAVEAT_placeholder_ratings.note: case118 ratings are the uniform 9,900 MVA PLACEHOLDERS already recorded in data/thermal_check.json as 'UNDEFINED (rating populated but PLACEHOLDER)'. pre_loading_percent therefore peaks at 6.03% and is NOT utilisation; it is the current magnitude divided by an arbitrary constant. The FLOW columns (pre_p_mw, pre_q_mvar, pre_i_ka) are physically real; loading_percent adds little beyond pre_i_ka on this network.

F2.note: pivot of the same artifact: pre_loading_percent for all 186 branches, identical across the 186 rows of a scenario

F3.source: pandapower.pypower.makeLODF on the base-case ppc branch array
F3.definition: exact DC line outage distribution factors: dF_l / F_k for the outage of branch k, from the linearized DC network. LODF is by construction a DC quantity; this is NOT an approximation of an AC quantity, it is the exact value of the DC quantity.
F3.constant_reason: depends only on branch series admittance and topology, neither of which varies across scenarios: generator outages change in_service on gens, not on branches

DEFECT_nan_cells.structure: column-structured: 7 of 186 columns carry every NaN
DEFECT_nan_cells.cause: LODF is undefined for an outage that ISLANDS the network: the denominator 1 - PTDF_kk is zero. case118 has 9 branches that are graph bridges; all 9 have a NaN self-term and 7 columns propagate NaN into other rows.
DEFECT_nan_cells.policy_required_before_partC: NOT DECIDED HERE. A fill (0 with a validity-indicator column) or a column drop must be chosen and stated. Silently filling NaN with 0 would assert that outaging a bridge redistributes nothing, which is false.

orientation_fix.defect: PART B used lodf[b, :] (monitored-branch row); correct is lodf[:, b]
orientation_fix.pypower_convention: LODF[l, k] = H[l,k] / (1 - h[k]); k = OUTAGED, l = MONITORED
orientation_fix.evidence: makeLODF builds den = ones*h.T*-1 + 1, constant DOWN each column

nonfinite.partB_undercount: PART B reported 663 (NaN only); +/-inf was missed

fill_policy.rule: row zero-filled when |1 - h[k]| < 1e-9 OR any cell non-finite
fill_policy.indicator_semantics: 1 = LODF row defined; 0 = outage islands the network and every entry was filled

reconciliation_9_vs_7.verdict: the count is 9 and the instruction was right. An earlier pass of this script tested only for non-finite cells, found 7, and wrongly concluded the other 2 held real values. They do not: den = 1.11e-16 for both, i.e. h[k] = 1 to machine precision, the islanding signature. Their entries are 0/0 that resolved to finite, plausible-looking numbers (max |LODF| 1.75 and 1.00) which are numerically arbitrary. All 9 are now zero-filled and flagged.
reconciliation_9_vs_7.corrected_from: an earlier verdict in this same file that said 7, not 9
